paper: Resilience and Asset Pricing in COVID-19 Disaster
core_thesis: Workplace resilience and financial resilience jointly determine how COVID-19 affected dividend growth and equity prices. Low-leverage firms with high operational flexibility suffer the least cash flow damage. Financial resilience (composite of leverage, liquidity, profitability) amplifies or dampens the workplace resilience effect. Low-leverage + high-profitability firms earn a persistent premium because their dividend growth is more stable under stress.
key_insights: Financial resilience (measured via DFPCA of corporate financials) amplifies workplace resilience: low-leverage high-quality firms outperform most in stress regimes
Analyst earnings expectations diverge most between high/low resilience firms — revision signals are stronger for low-leverage firms
The interaction of leverage and earnings quality (accruals) predicts cross-sectional returns: high accrual + high leverage = worst outcome
The dividend growth model implies: rank(financial_resilience) predicts returns cross-sectionally beyond simple leverage or quality alone
Firms with leverage above 80th pct and low workplace resilience saw the sharpest earnings expectation cuts — this creates a persistent reversal opportunity
failure_modes: Signal is regime-dependent: strongest in high-uncertainty / stress periods (COVID, GFC); weaker in pure bull markets
Leverage-quality interaction may be slow-moving (quarterly rebalancing); low turnover kills fitness without a price-based leg

hypotheses.name: financial_resilience_composite
hypotheses.claim: Firms with low leverage AND high profitability (financially resilient firms) earn a persistent equity premium because their dividend streams are more stable under macroeconomic stress.
hypotheses.mechanism: fundamental — financial resilience (Daadmehr 2024): leverage dampens the benefit of high profitability; the composite signal ranks firms on BOTH dimensions simultaneously, capturing the interaction the paper documents
hypotheses.field_rationale: ebit/assets = return on assets (profitability leg); debt/assets = leverage ratio (solvency leg); rank both and take the difference to get the composite resilience score

prediction.regime_fails: strong bull markets where leverage amplifies returns rather than risk

hypotheses.refutation_criterion: composite outperforms either profitability or leverage alone (IC > individual legs); if not, the interaction is not additive

hypotheses.name: leverage_amplified_accruals_reversal
hypotheses.claim: High-accrual, high-leverage firms are doubly mispriced: investors over-extrapolate inflated earnings AND ignore the fragility of high-leverage balance sheets. The joint signal predicts the sharpest negative returns.
hypotheses.mechanism: behavioral + fundamental — Daadmehr (2024) shows leverage amplifies cash flow damage; Sloan (1996) shows accrual mispricing; combining them targets the intersection of overvalued earnings quality AND fragile balance sheet
hypotheses.field_rationale: accrual proxy = ts_delta(ebit/assets) deviation from long-run mean; leverage = debt/equity; short the high-accrual high-leverage firms

prediction.regime_works: post-earnings periods; stress regimes where leverage amplification is priced
prediction.regime_fails: liquidity-driven rallies where leverage adds return before it adds risk

hypotheses.refutation_criterion: interaction term (accruals × leverage) IC > max(accruals_IC, leverage_IC) individually; if not, signals are redundant

hypotheses.name: resilience_quality_vwap_reversal
hypotheses.claim: Financially resilient firms (high profitability, low leverage) that experience intraday price weakness (close < vwap) present mean-reversion opportunities because temporary sell pressure is unrelated to their strong fundamentals.
hypotheses.mechanism: fundamental × microstructure — Daadmehr (2024) establishes the cross-sectional fundamental premium; VWAP deviation adds a timing leg that increases turnover and fitness. The reversal is faster for high-quality firms because liquidity providers quickly correct the dislocation.
hypotheses.field_rationale: quality score = rank(ebit/assets) - rank(debt/assets); VWAP deviation = -(close-vwap)/vwap as reversal signal; gate quality firms on intraday weakness
hypotheses.expression: group_neutralize(rank(ts_decay_linear((rank(ebit / ts_delay(assets, 1)) - rank(debt / ts_delay(assets, 1))) * rank(-(close - vwap) / vwap), 6)), subindustry)

prediction.regime_works: normal markets with moderate volatility; works best when fundamental quality is priced
prediction.regime_fails: momentum-dominant regimes; high-volatility crises where even quality names gap lower

hypotheses.refutation_criterion: IC of combined signal > max(quality_only_IC, vwap_reversal_IC); if the quality gate adds no lift over raw VWAP reversal, the fundamental layer is not needed

hypotheses.name: declining_leverage_earnings_acceleration
hypotheses.claim: Firms simultaneously deleveraging AND improving profitability earn the strongest forward returns — the double positive signal from Daadmehr's financial resilience index. Leverage decline frees up cash flow that accrues to equity holders while improving earnings quality reduces the accrual overhang.
hypotheses.mechanism: fundamental — Daadmehr (2024) financial resilience: the most resilient firms show improving profitability AND declining leverage simultaneously; this combination has the most stable dividend growth and the lowest subsequent analyst earnings disappointment
hypotheses.field_rationale: deleveraging = -ts_delta(debt, 252)/ts_delay(assets, 252) (declining debt/assets is positive); profitability acceleration = ts_delta(ebit/sales, 63) (improving margins is positive); both are long-horizon fundamental signals smoothed for turnover

prediction.regime_works: recovery periods after stress events; works best when credit market conditions normalize
prediction.regime_fails: periods of forced deleveraging where balance sheet repair is priced in already

hypotheses.refutation_criterion: long-short IC positive (long deleveraging+improving margin firms, short increasing leverage+declining margin); sign should be consistent across sectors

hypotheses.name: leverage_gated_sales_efficiency_momentum
hypotheses.claim: Firms improving sales efficiency (sales/assets rising) while keeping leverage low earn positive returns because they are generating organic growth without financial risk amplification — the ideal Daadmehr financial resilience profile.
hypotheses.mechanism: fundamental — sales/assets captures asset turnover efficiency; the leverage gate ensures only firms with sustainable improvement (not leveraged buybacks) are selected; this mirrors the paper's finding that low-leverage firms with positive fundamental momentum outperform most persistently
hypotheses.field_rationale: sales/assets = asset turnover; ts_delta over 126d captures improving trajectory; debt/equity gate filters to low-leverage subset; smoothed with decay for turnover control

prediction.regime_works: post-recession recoveries; periods of broad fundamental improvement; works year-round as quality factor
prediction.regime_fails: late-cycle leverage-driven expansions where high-leverage firms temporarily outperform on price momentum

hypotheses.refutation_criterion: low-leverage gate improves IC vs ungated sales efficiency signal; if the gate reduces IC, leverage amplification is not the mechanism in current data
